hints: Halve the coefficient of $x$ to form a squared bracket, then adjust the constant term.
walkthrough:
Complete the square for $f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 3$:
$$f(x) = (x - 2)^2 - 4 + 3 = (x - 2)^2 - 1$$
where $a = 2$ and $b = -1$.

hints: For $f(x)$ to be one-to-one, the domain $x > c$ must be strictly to one side of the vertex $x = 2$.
walkthrough:
The quadratic curve $y = (x - 2)^2 - 1$ has its line of symmetry and turning point at $x = 2$.
For $f(x)$ to be a strictly increasing one-to-one function on $x > c$, the domain must begin at or after the turning point:
$$\text{Smallest value of } c = 2$$

Set $y = (x - 2)^2 - 1$ and solve for $x$:
$$(x - 2)^2 = y + 1 \implies x - 2 = \sqrt{y + 1} \implies x = 2 + \sqrt{y + 1}$$
$$f^{-1}(x) = 2 + \sqrt{x + 1}$$

Determine the domain of $f^{-1}$ from the range of $f$ on $x > 5$:
$$x > 5 \implies f(x) > (5 - 2)^2 - 1 = 9 - 1 = 8$$
$$\text{Domain of } f^{-1}: \quad x > 8 \quad (\text{or } (8, \infty))$$

Determine the range of $gf(x)$ on the domain $x > 5$:
$$x > 5 \implies x - 2 > 3 \implies (x - 2)^2 > 9$$
$$\text{Taking reciprocals: } \quad 0 < \frac{1}{(x - 2)^2} < \frac{1}{9}$$
$$\text{Range of } gf: \quad 0 < gf(x) < \frac{1}{9} \quad \left(\text{or } \left(0, \frac{1}{9}\right)\right)$$
